1.e4 e5 2.Nf3 Nc6 3.Nc3 Nf6 4.Bb5 Bb4.name: Four Knights Game: Spanish Variation, Double Spanish
1.e4 e5 2.Nf3 Nc6 3.Nc3 Nf6 4.Bb5 Bb4.background: Black's most common reply to 4.Bb5 and the main line today. It has been played by Nigel Short, Michael Adams and Alexei Shirov, among others.

1.e4 e5 2.Nf3 Nc6 3.Nc3 Nf6 4.Bb5 Bb4 5..strategy: Gets the king to safety and out of the b4-bishop's diagonal, so a pin on the c3 knight can never become awkward. White keeps the symmetry, and the bishop on b5 keeps leaning on the c6 knight.

Mirrors White once more: Black's king is as safe as White's, and every plan on one side has an equivalent on the other. The game stays balanced and strategic, and the first side to deviate takes on the risk of unbalancing it.
